findings.summary: The mandatory baseline execution record's output digest is never bound to the packet's expected baseline commit, so a fabricated output_sha256 passes verification.
findings.evidence: libexec/harness-claude-handoff:502-508 checks only that the 'baseline' record has command ['git','rev-parse','HEAD'] and exit_status 0; the output_sha256 is validated only as 64 hex characters. tests/test-claude-handoff.sh:196,323-343 uses the placeholder digest 'ddd…d' for that record and both verify-evidence and driver reproduction pass (asserted at lines 354-356), because validate_reproduction (lines 446-459) also only compares JSON fields without recomputing anything.
findings.recommendation: Define the execution-record output encoding convention (for example SHA-256 over the exact stdout bytes 'COMMIT\n') and have verify-evidence require the baseline record's output_sha256 to equal the digest derived from the expected baseline commit; otherwise document explicitly that this binding rests on driver reproduction honesty.

findings.summary: Three validator refusal paths in verify-evidence have no negative test coverage: read-manifest mismatch, recovered-field mismatch, and stage-inputs/source_files set mismatch.
findings.evidence: tests/test-claude-handoff.sh exercises prompt receipt mismatch (line 270), forbidden execution records (line 276), stale staged bytes (line 358), missing reproduction (line 364), and the broken-sandbox case (line 385), but no assertion triggers 'read manifest does not match the sealed stage' (libexec/harness-claude-handoff:324), 'recovered handoff does not match the packet' (line 443), or 'stage inputs differ from packet source files' (line 373).
findings.recommendation: Add one focused negative assertion per untested refusal path (drop or alter one read-manifest row, mutate one recovered field, and add or remove one stage input) so regressions in these gates are caught by the focused suite.

findings.summary: The public retry schema is laxer than the validator: previous_run_id and next_run_id are unconstrained strings while the validator enforces the run-identity pattern.
findings.evidence: docs/schemas/claude-handoff-retry.schema.json:23-24 declares {'type': 'string'} with no pattern, but libexec/harness-claude-handoff:539-543 rejects run identities not matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$; the packet and evidence schemas both carry that pattern for run_id, so the retry schema under-documents the accepted contract (safe direction, validator is stricter).
findings.recommendation: Add the same run-identity pattern to previous_run_id and next_run_id in the public retry schema so the documented contract matches the enforced one.

residual_risks: Limit of evidence: this review ran under Read/Grep/Glob only, so no SHA-256 digest or git query was independently recomputed; stage.json input digests, the frozen retest result digest 224eb5d8…, staged-versus-live source freshness, and the packet baseline 213c8f72… being the repository HEAD were consistency-checked across records, not rehashed. Driver-side verify-evidence remains the binding check.

Limit of evidence: an echoed read manifest proves receipt of the sealed digest map, not complete byte-level reading of every source; complete-read compliance is self-reported by the copilot, an accepted contract limitation recorded in docs/audits/t343-claude-handoff-hardening/cowork/execution.md.

Limit of evidence: TODO.md (391 KB) exceeds the read window; the header, T-343, and adjacent T-342/T-341 sections were read in full and the remainder was searched for T-343/handoff/Fable references only, finding no contradictions.

Limit of evidence: execution-class trust ultimately rests on the driver honestly authoring the reproduction receipt after a real re-run; the validator is a consistency gate, not an executor, so it cannot detect a colluding or careless driver.

Potential future defect (not demonstrated): tests/test-claude-handoff.sh:53 uses ast.parse feature_version=(3, 6); newer CPython releases have been raising the minimum supported feature_version, so the 3.6 syntax gate's behavior on future interpreters is unverified here.

Implementation state, not a defect: acceptance is not yet claimable — benchmark scoring of the eight cases, import of this final critique, the final clean full-suite repetition, protected publication, and live ruleset/fleet readback remain pending per validation.md and the TODO.md next action.
